food.name: Brussels Sprouts

identity.basisReason: The raw per-100g identity is the canonical whole-food entry; roasting, steaming, shredding, and boiling are preparation guidance rather than separate entries.
includes: the same sprouts prepared at home without becoming a separate product identity
excludes: Brussels sprouts cooked with bacon, oil, glaze, or sauce

scoreReadiness.summary: Complete per-100g raw Brussels-sprout profile using exact USDA nutrients, an exact-food amino-acid record, and a documented category digestibility estimate.
caveats: Protein digestibility is a documented other-vegetables category estimate, not an exact Brussels-sprout measurement.
Glycemic index is a contextual estimate rather than a universal exact-food laboratory value.
Variety, season, storage, and cooking method can change the realised nutrient profile.

sourceNotes: Production-safe raw whole-food entry scored per 100g.
USDA Foundation FDC 2685575 supplies the primary macro profile and vitamin C; USDA SR Legacy FDC 170383 fills missing fat, vitamin, and mineral rows.
The Japanese food-composition record supplies an exact raw Brussels-sprout amino-acid profile.
The 65% protein-digestibility value is a documented WHO other-vegetables category estimate rather than an exact Brussels-sprout measurement.

topPros.title: glucosinolate-rich brassica profile
topPros.explanation: Brussels sprouts have a food-specific glucosinolate story beyond the visible vitamin bars.

topPros.explanation: They add useful plate volume without making the meal heavy.

explanation.summary: Carbs are carrying this food most, while minerals are holding it back most. It lands in A tier.

closing.summary: Best bits are fibre, low glycemic impact, vitamins C and K, and the glucosinolate profile. Weak spots are useful fat, useful amino-acid amounts, minerals, and digestive tolerance. Best for digestion, immune support, bone support, and low-calorie volume because the fibre helps the gut, the vitamins do real work, and it adds a lot to a plate without much energy.
